title: The PAP Therapy Equipment Coverage Trial: Compliance and Practitioner Re-Evaluation
content:
# The PAP Therapy Equipment Coverage Trial

**The trial.** A coverage-billed PAP Therapy Equipment device starts on a trial of the class's trial length, counted from the setup date as day 1.

**Scoring a window.** A compliance download scores one window of the class's compliance window of consecutive nights. *This clause is no longer in force for a usage summary download, which is governed by the current basis; every other compliance download remains a scored window under it.* Under the nights-over-threshold basis the window is met when the nights of at least the class's minimum hours are at least the class's share-of-nights percentage of the nights in the window — that is, when those nights multiplied by 100 reach at least the share multiplied by the nights in the window. Under the average-daily-use basis the window is met when the average daily use hours are at least the class's minimum hours.

**Evidence of use.** Where the class proves compliance only from modem or card data, only modem or card data count, never the patient's own account of use.

**Conversion.** The trial converts to active rental only when both proofs are on file: a met window ending no later than the class's latest window end day, and a practitioner re-evaluation whose visit date falls between the class's earliest and latest re-evaluation days inclusive with benefit documented. A device is converted only when a compliance download on this device record shows the compliance result met and a practitioner re-evaluation received on this device record shows benefit documented. Both are read from this device record's service history as the system holds them, before the conversion.

**Failed trial.** A trial without both proofs by its last day fails: rental months from month 4 are not billable and are denied with "compliance not documented" or "re-evaluation missing" when submitted, and a new trial needs the class's requirement after a failed trial.

## Conversion at a glance

| Met window on this record, ending no later than the latest end day | Re-evaluation on this record within the day range, benefit documented | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | converts to active rental |
| yes | no | not converted |
| no | yes | not converted |
| no | no | not converted |

## Worked windows (hypothetical downloads)

- Nights over threshold, share 70: 30 nights in the window, 22 nights of 4 hours or more. 22 multiplied by 100 is 2200; 70 multiplied by 30 is 2100; 2200 reaches 2100, so the window is met. With 20 such nights, 2000 falls short and the window is not met.
- Average daily use, minimum 4 hours: an average of 4.1 hours is met; 3.8 hours is not.

**Re-evaluation range (hypothetical dates).** With the setup date on 1 March as trial day 1, trial day 31 is 31 March and trial day 91 is 30 May. On a CPAP class whose range runs from day 31 to day 91, visits on 31 March and on 30 May both fall in the range; a visit on 30 March does not.
